To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
4H syndrome is caused by mutations in POLR3 genes, and the POLR3 genes are located on chromosome 3.
a novel homozygote mutation in the exon 18 of POLR3A is responsible for 4H syndrome in our patient.
a novel homozygote mutation in the POL3A gene has been reported in an Indian patient with clinical features of 4H syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic basis of a rare congenital leukodystrophy.
the identification of a novel mutation in the exon 18 of POLR3A in a 4H syndrome patient and her parents.
a case report of 4H syndrome in a 1½-year-old child from India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient is suffering from 4H syndrome due to novel homozygosity of mutation in POLR 3A gene.
this is a case of 4H syndrome due to homozygous POLR3A mutation.
this is the first case from India with 4H syndrome due to homozygous novel mutation in the exon 18 of POLR3A.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the POLR3 gene mutations should be considered in the differential diagnosis of children presenting with developmental delay, hypomyelinating brain lesions, hypodontia and hypogonadal features.

POLR3A mutations are rare in India and the novel homozygote mutation identified in this patient may be a new variant in the POLR 3A gene.
